items.title: Does generative AI narrow education-based productivity gaps? Evidence from a randomized experiment
items.desc: A randomized online experiment with 1,174 adults finds a generative-AI assistant improves performance for everyone but helps less-educated workers most, shrinking the education productivity gap from 0.548 to 0.139 standard deviations. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-04]

items.title: Optimal Liability Design for Medical AI
items.desc: A principal-agent model in which a planner sets medical-liability rules for a physician of unobservable quality who must choose between standard treatment, personalized judgment, or following an imperfect AI recommendation, yielding new insights on regulating AI-assisted care. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-08-04]

items.title: The Fallback as Signal: Preserved Human Skill, Liability, and Competence Signaling in Credence-Good Markets under Improving AI
items.desc: Models how firms deploying improving but imperfect AI decide how much to keep human workers engaged; an agent-based version reproduces the analytical thresholds under noisy beliefs, learning-by-record, and worker churn. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-08-04]

items.title: Revealed Rationality: Label-Free Evaluation and Regularization from Representation Theorems
items.desc: Argues that decision-theory representation theorems offer a label-free way to evaluate and regularize LLMs and other AI systems, checking axiom compliance directly from a model's own responses to synthetic choice problems. [arXiv econ.TH, posted 2026-08-05]

items.title: From Financial Sentiment Classification to Return Predictability: A QLoRA Benchmark of Large Language Models
items.desc: Benchmarks TF-IDF, FinBERT, Financial-RoBERTa, and QLoRA-adapted Qwen2.5, LLaMA3, and Mistral LLMs on financial sentiment, showing that strong classification accuracy does not necessarily translate into economically useful return predictability. [arXiv q-fin.MF, posted 2026-08-04]

items.title: Adaptive Finite-Budget Training for CVaR Risk-Aware Q-Learning
items.desc: Proposes an adaptive training controller for Conditional Value-at-Risk risk-aware Q-learning that stabilizes value estimates under limited sample budgets, evaluated on a daily Bitcoin trading task. [arXiv q-fin.RM / cs.LG, posted 2026-08-05]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Discretion in Automated Supermarket Replenishment: Censorship Bias and Self-Inflicted Stockouts
items.desc: Using perishable-goods data from a supermarket chain, the paper shows that managers who deviate downward from an automated replenishment system's proposals after a stockout suffer from censorship bias, hurting inventory performance and revealing pitfalls of human discretion over algorithmic recommendations. [M&SOM, Published Online 2026-08-05]

items.title: India's IT sector is surviving artificial intelligence
items.desc: Despite fears that AI would gut India's roughly 6-million-strong IT industry by automating software development and routine business processes, hard evidence of job losses is scarce so far, though the technology is making the graduate job market tougher. [Economist, 2026-08-06]

items.title: Governments are making a dangerous bet on the AI boom
items.desc: The Economist argues rich-world governments are relying on AI-fueled growth to repair strained public finances, but 30-year bond yields near post-financial-crisis highs suggest markets doubt the bet will pay off. [Economist, 2026-08-05]

items.title: China's AI drive threatens the world's largest workforce
items.desc: As China promotes AI adoption, its leaders worry about displacement; ByteDance's Seedance video model has cut microdrama production up to 90% cheaper, halving some workers' wages and drying up gigs. [Economist, 2026-08-06]

items.title: The A.I. Jargon That Will Help You Spot a Stock Downturn
items.desc: An opinion column by economist Rebecca Patterson decodes four AI-industry concepts that reveal whether Big Tech's nearly $1 trillion in projected AI capital spending can earn enough revenue to justify valuations and avoid a market crash. [NYT, 2026-08-06]

items.title: China's Robots Know Kung Fu and Can Scale Walls. Can They Woo Investors?
items.desc: Chinese robotics maker Unitree is seeking about $900 million in an IPO that tests investor appetite for humanoid robots, an AI-driven technology that impresses but has yet to prove commercial viability. [NYT, 2026-08-06]

items.title: The Winners of Trump's A.I. Safety Plan
items.desc: DealBook analyzes how the Trump administration's new AI safety-review guidelines appear to exempt Chinese AI models while subjecting US firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic to scrutiny. [NYT, 2026-08-05]

items.title: Google's stock drops after Nobel-winning AI executive steps aside
items.desc: Google shares fell after Demis Hassabis, the Nobel-winning DeepMind co-founder who led all of Google's AI work, stepped aside to focus on AI-for-science, a shake-up that comes as Google faces pressure to keep pace in the AI race. [Washington Post, 2026-08-05]
